cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the saints in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He just said it's the doers of the law, not just the hearers, who will be declared righteous (Romans 2:13). Now he turns and talks straight to you, if you call yourself a Jew.

cards.question: Paul goes on: if you rely on something and boast in God. What does Paul say you rely on?

cards.text: Paul's list of ifs keeps going: if you know God's will and approve of what is superior, because the law instructs you. If you're convinced you're a guide for the blind…

cards.question: In Paul's list, the one who calls himself a Jew is also convinced he's a light for those in darkness.

cards.text: Paul adds: if you're convinced you're an instructor of the foolish and a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth. Guide, light, instructor, teacher. That's FOUR titles, friend. I've got ONE, Papa, and I had to ask an angel if I could keep it.

cards.question: After that whole list, Paul turns it around on the one who teaches others. What does Paul ask him?

answers.text: Do you not learn from others
Do you not test your students

cards.question: Paul asks the one who preaches against stealing whether he steals.
Paul asks the one who abhors idols if he robs temples. And what does Paul ask the one who forbids adultery?
Paul asks the one who boasts in the law: by breaking the law, do you ___ God?

cards.text: Paul's point is like me hanging a big NO TASTING THE DOUGH sign while there's dough all over my mustache. Then Paul quotes Scripture about what this does to God's name.

cards.question: Paul quotes Scripture saying God's name is blasphemed because of these lawbreakers. Among whom?

cards.text: Next Paul brings up circumcision, the sign of the covenant God gave Abraham and his descendants (Genesis 17:10-11). Hold onto your apron, friend, because Paul's about to say what that sign is really worth.

cards.question: Paul says circumcision has value on one condition. What is it?
Paul says if you break the law, your circumcision still counts as circumcision.

cards.text: Now Paul flips the whole thing over. Picture a man who isn't circumcised, but he keeps the requirements of the law.

cards.question: Paul asks about the uncircumcised man who keeps the requirements of the law. His uncircumcision will be regarded as what?
Paul says the physically uncircumcised man who keeps the law will ___ the lawbreaker who has the written code and circumcision.

cards.text: Then Paul says a man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, and circumcision isn't only outward and physical. A box with a big bow on it and NOTHING inside? That's not a cookie box, friend.

cards.question: Paul says a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the ___, by the ___, not by the written code.
Paul says a man who is a Jew inwardly gets his praise from other people.

findings.problem: The card's references to "Guide" and "light," and its count of four titles, use Romans 2:19 as well as Romans 2:20. The citation should therefore span Romans 2:19-20 rather than citing only verse 20.
